policy_title: Improve Access to Arts, Music, and Sport
stated: Labour will implement their creative industries sector plan to create jobs and growth. They will support children to study creative or vocational subjects until age 16, protect time for physical education, and support grassroots clubs. Publicly funded national museums and galleries will be required to increase loans to communities. A new National Music Education Network will provide information on courses and classes. New consumer protections on ticket resales will put fans first. Labour will also reform football governance by establishing an independent regulator to ensure financial sustainability and prevent closed leagues.

source.quote: Labour will implement our creative industries sector plan as part of our Industrial Strategy, creating good jobs and accelerating growth in film, music, gaming, and other creative sectors. Labour will support children to study a creative or vocational subject until they are 16, and ensure accountability measures reflect this. We will get more children active by protecting time for physical education, and supporting the role grassroots clubs play in expanding access to sport. Labour will improve access to cultural assets by requiring publicly funded national museums and galleries to increase the loans they make from their collections to communities across the country. We will also launch a new National Music Education Network – a one-stop shop with information on courses and classes for parents, teachers and children. Access to music, drama and sport has become difficult and expensive because of ticket touting. Labour will put fans back at the heart of events by introducing new consumer protections on ticket resales. Labour is committed to making Britain the best place in the world to be a football fan. We will reform football governance to protect football clubs across our communities and to give fans a greater say in the way they are run. We will introduce a Football Governance Bill, which will establish an independent regulator to ensure financial sustainability of football clubs in England. We will never allow a closed league of select clubs to be siphoned off from the English football pyramid.

bearing_set.reason: Mandating creative/vocational subjects to age 16, protecting PE time, and creating a National Music Education Network directly shape school curriculum content, attainment breadth, and access to arts and skills education—earning a real verdict on school standards and opportunity.

An explicit creative industries sector plan targeting job creation, combined with football governance reform designed to ensure club financial sustainability, bears non-negligibly on employment quality and security in those sectors.

The creative industries sector plan is explicitly aimed at 'jobs and growth' in a sector the DCMS values at over £100bn; a targeted sector plan can materially affect productivity, business dynamism, and economic opportunity in that sector.

Supporting grassroots clubs, mandating museum loans to communities, and protecting PE time are direct mechanisms for civic participation, inter-group contact, and sense of community belonging — the primary O15 indicators.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: the education strand (O7), the economic/sector-growth strand (O13), and the community participation strand (O15). Ticket resale protections and football governance are consumer/regulatory measures whose fiscal and liberty effects do not plausibly move any single fundamental's indicators to a non-negligible degree on their own.
